cf.title: Fix for bug #19773 : pg_dump differing generation expressions of inherited columns

input.subject: [PATCH v1] Fix for bug #19773 : pg_dump differing generation expressions of inherited columns

verdict_reasoning: The goal is a reported bug fix (#19773) for wrong restores that report no error, and no surviving objection questions the goal or the v2 approach. The one surviving objection, replication-ondisk-1, concerns commit order. Messages #2 and #6 show that the emitted SET EXPRESSION drops a child's inherited CHECK and NOT NULL rows, and the thread does not say whether the backpatch to 17 waits for the backend fix. A committer who knows pg_dump and the stable branches has to decide that.

brief.title: pg_dump: dump differing generation expressions of inherited columns
brief.problem: pg_dump drops a child table's generation expression when it differs from the parent's, so the restored child silently uses the parent's expression and computes wrong values (bug #19773). The state became possible in v16, and since v17 ALTER TABLE ... SET EXPRESSION can produce it on an inherited column. Users of table inheritance with generated columns are affected.
brief.proposed_design: pg_dump emits a separate ALTER TABLE ONLY ... SET EXPRESSION for a child whose column is not printed, as it does for defaults. It does so when the child's expression differs from the parent's, or when it matches but the parent's expression is itself dumped separately. v2 makes that second decision after sorting the dumpable objects instead of adding dependency edges, because v1's edges caused sort hangs.
user_visible_surface: pg_dump output now contains ALTER TABLE ONLY ... ALTER COLUMN ... SET EXPRESSION AS (...) for inherited generated columns.
author_claims: Fixes the reported cases for STORED and VIRTUAL columns; the reviewer confirmed this for v1.
v2 fixes the sort hang and the multi-level cases where the child silently got the old parent expression.
Checking after the sort is cleaner and easier to maintain than adding new loop-repair rules.
Always emitting SET EXPRESSION at the end was rejected because restore to v16 and older lacks that command.
brief.thread_state: Henson Choi reviewed v1 and v2, found the v2 approach sound, and leaves the multi-parent case and the loss of inherited CHECK and NOT NULL constraints on SET EXPRESSION as separate backend bugs, which the author will take up. Ashutosh Bapat suggests testing through 002_pg_upgrade, and jian he points to known SET EXPRESSION dependency problems; neither point has an answer yet.
unclear: Restores with v2 lose inherited CHECK and NOT NULL constraints on children because SET EXPRESSION drops them; the thread does not say whether this patch should wait for the backend fix.
The thread does not say whether the backpatch to 17 depends on a backpatched backend fix.
The author has not replied on moving tests to 002_pg_upgrade or on the SET EXPRESSION dependency issues jian he linked.
Henson Choi's request to rename maybe_dump_later_if_altered_expression has no reply yet.
The multi-parent case still fails at restore, here and on master, with no plan stated.

objections.title: Patch makes dump/restore produce inconsistent inherited-constraint catalog state
objections.failure_scenario: A v17 user with an inherited CHECK or NOT NULL on a generated column dumps with a patched pg_dump and restores. The restore reports no error, but the child's pg_constraint rows are missing, so rows that violate the CHECK are accepted. Later, pg_upgrade of that cluster passes --check and then fails with "child table is missing constraint", and DROP NOT NULL on the parent fails with "cache lookup failed".
objections.argument: Message #2 and message #6 show that the emitted ALTER TABLE ONLY ... SET EXPRESSION drops inherited CHECK and NOT NULL rows through ATPostAlterTypeCleanup(). The bug is in the backend, but today pg_dump never emits that command, so ordinary dump/restore does not hit it; the patch would make every such dump hit it. Today the child gets the wrong expression; with the patch it gets the right expression and a catalog that a later pg_upgrade rejects. The thread does not say whether the patch waits for the backend fix, or whether that fix will be backpatched to 17.
objections.author_must_show: Will this go in only together with a backend SET EXPRESSION fix, backpatched to 17, so that no released minor version restores into a catalog that pg_upgrade later rejects?

precedents.title: Revert "Improve compression and storage support with inheritance"

critic.reasoning: Messages #2 and #6 show that v2 restores drop inherited CHECK constraints without an error, and the thread does not say whether the backpatch waits for the backend fix. P18 reverted a backend feature and must not be used as support.

refuted.title: Inheritance dump fix tested only in pg_dump TAP, not pg_upgrade
refuted.failure_scenario: A later backend change, such as the planned SET EXPRESSION constraint fix, creates a new inheritance state that this patch's rules do not handle. The cases sit only in 002_pg_dump.pl, so the regression database never holds them and 002_pg_upgrade does not round-trip them. A user finds the wrong expression or missing constraint after restore.
refuted.argument: [P18] reverted an inheritance feature because pg_dump could not dump every structure it allowed and coverage was lacking, and [P1] cited "unexpected pitfalls and lacking test coverage". Here the reviewer found three silent wrong-restore cases in v1 (message #2) and inherited constraint loss in v2 (message #6), which shows the area has such pitfalls. Message #7 asks for coverage through 002_pg_upgrade and has no reply, and v2 still adds only pg_dump TAP tests.
refuted.author_must_show: Can the cases from messages #2 and #6 be left in the regression database so 002_pg_upgrade checks expressions and inherited constraints after restore?

precedents.title: Revert "Improve compression and storage support with inheritance"
table inheritance versus column compression and storage settings

critic.reasoning: The scenario depends on an unnamed future backend change, and where the tests live is a level 4 matter outside this review. P18 and P1 concern a backend feature that pg_dump could not dump, so they do not support this objection about a pg_dump fix.

refuted.title: Restores with v2 lose inherited CHECK and NOT NULL constraints
refuted.failure_scenario: A user on 17 with a CHECK on a parent and a child whose expression was changed upgrades to a fixed minor release, then dumps and restores. The restore reports no error, but the child has no inherited CHECK row, so rows that violate it are accepted. A later pg_upgrade passes --check and then fails with "child table is missing constraint".
refuted.argument: Message #2 and message #6 show that every SET EXPRESSION the patch emits drops the child's inherited CHECK and NOT NULL rows. Today the bad state is wrong values. After the patch it becomes missing constraints and catalog damage, such as "cache lookup failed for not-null constraint" on DROP NOT NULL. Henson calls this a separate backend bug, and that is fair as a cause, but the thread does not say whether this patch, backpatched to 17, waits for that fix or ships before it. A committer would likely not backpatch a dump change that introduces a new silent loss.
refuted.author_must_show: Will this patch be committed and backpatched only together with a backend fix that keeps inherited CHECK and NOT NULL constraints on SET EXPRESSION in 17 and later?

precedents.title: Revert "Improve compression and storage support with inheritance"

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which states the same constraint loss and the same commit-order question more completely.

refuted.title: Backpatched dumps would trade wrong expressions for lost inherited constraints
refuted.failure_scenario: A v17 user with a CHECK or NOT NULL on a parent and a changed child expression dumps and restores with the next minor release. The restore succeeds without error, but the children have no inherited constraint rows and accept rows the source rejects. A later pg_upgrade passes --check and then fails with "child table is missing constraint".
refuted.argument: Message #2 and message #6 show that every SET EXPRESSION the patch emits for a child drops that child's inherited CHECK and NOT NULL rows, and message #6 shows DROP NOT NULL then fails with "cache lookup failed". Henson calls this a separate backend bug, and that is fair. But the patch is the first thing that makes plain dump/restore run that command, and the backend fix has no posted patch. If the backpatch to 17 lands first, minor releases ship a new silent catalog corruption, and that is harder to undo than the current bug.
refuted.author_must_show: Will the backend fix for inherited CHECK and NOT NULL loss on SET EXPRESSION be committed and backpatched to 17 before or together with this pg_dump change?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which covers the same constraint loss and the same question about the order of the two fixes.

refuted.title: Post-sort decision adds a second, generation-only path beside defaults
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch changes dependency loop repair, or adds another case where an attrdef becomes separate. It does not know that flagInhGenerationExprs must also see that change. Children are then created before the parent's SET EXPRESSION and silently inherit the old expression, with no pg_dump error or warning.
refuted.argument: v2 lets loop repair decide separate during sorting, then makes a second decision after sorting, through a new AttrDefInfo field (message #4). Correctness now depends on the two passes staying consistent, and nothing in pg_dump fails loudly when they do not. Defaults have the same multi-level limitation (message #4) but keep the old path, so the two attrdef kinds now follow different rules. No committer has engaged, and Ashutosh's suggestion to cover the states through 002_pg_upgrade so later DDL changes are caught has no reply (message #7).
refuted.author_must_show: Which test would fail if a future change to loop repair, or to attrdef handling, made an expression separate without flagInhGenerationExprs noticing it?

precedents.title: Revert "Improve compression and storage support with inheritance"

critic.reasoning: The commit message says the decision runs after sorting because loop repair can make an expression separate, so the check sees that case by design. Message #4 weighed new loop-repair rules and rejected them as harder to maintain, and it ties the defaults limitation to the multi-parent case only.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: pg_upgrade uses pg_dump, and a restored cluster with missing inherited constraint rows later fails pg_upgrade with "child table is missing constraint".

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: see objection replication-ondisk-1: Patch makes dump/restore produce inconsistent inherited-constraint catalog state

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: pg_dump now emits ALTER TABLE ONLY ... SET EXPRESSION for inherited generated columns, which changes what a restore produces.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The commit message says "Backpatch-through: 17", and the emitted command triggers a backend bug that has no posted fix.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: v2 adds a decision after sortDumpableObjects() that only generation expressions use, next to the existing path for defaults.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Will this patch be committed and backpatched to 17 only together with a backend fix that keeps inherited CHECK and NOT NULL constraints on SET EXPRESSION?
Will the backend fix for constraint loss on SET EXPRESSION itself be backpatched to 17, or only applied to master?
What is the plan for the multi-parent case, which still fails at restore with v2 and on master?
Do the SET EXPRESSION dependency problems that jian he linked affect any command that v2 now emits in a dump?
Can the cases from messages #2 and #6 stay in the regression database so that 002_pg_upgrade checks them, as message #7 suggests?

committability.owner_note: It needs a committer who knows pg_dump's dependency sorting and inheritance handling, and who can judge backpatch risk for the stable branches. None has spoken in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for changed pg_dump output in 17 and later, including pg_upgrade runs. Until the backend fix lands, the owner also signs for restores that drop inherited CHECK and NOT NULL rows without an error.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 after the v1 review, and the brief says the author will take up the two backend bugs.

priority.reason: The bug affects only inheritance trees with differing generation expressions, but the restore gives wrong values without an error, so it merits a fix. The patch is about 20 KiB in pg_dump only; the open point is commit order with the backend fix.

provisional_note: Without the code, this review could not check that the decision made after sorting covers every case where loop repair makes an expression separate. It also could not check how the patch behaves for the multi-parent case.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: table inheritance versus column compression and storage settings
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change how MergeAttributes() handles column compression and storage settings under table inheritance, treating them as physical per-table properties. A new child inherits the parent's settings but can override them, attaching a child changes nothing, and conflicting settings from multiple parents require an explicit setting in the child.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The committed patch was reverted after Tom Lane showed that pg_dump and pg_restore of the regression database fail: stchild4 does not restore and stchild5 gets the wrong attstorage. Ashutosh Bapat then found related existing dump bugs and proposed setting defaults when parents conflict. Peter Eisentraut declined to take on that change late in the cycle, citing unexpected pitfalls, missing test coverage and no patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
We have already discovered with the previous attempt that
there are unexpected pitfalls and lacking test coverage.  Also, there
isn't even a patch yet.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_dump: optimize dumpFunc()
precedents_retrieved.summary: Replace pg_dump's per-function query in dumpFunc() with a single query that gathers data for all functions up front, keeping the PGresult in memory and using a sorted array of function OIDs to locate each function's row. The aim was to reduce dump time for databases with many functions (shown as about 0.25s to about 0.11s for 10k simple functions).
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane questioned whether the change helps databases with few functions and what it does to pg_dump's memory requirements when there are very many functions with large source text, and said the shown results did not justify the risk. The author agreed and withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm not sure that the results you're showing justify taking any
risk here.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve pg_dump dumping publication tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes pg_dump's getPublicationTables() to fetch all publication-table memberships with a single query, instead of iterating over every table and issuing a separate query per table. The matching TableInfo for each row is then looked up in tblinfoindex, which should be faster when there are many tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was superseded, not rejected: Tom Lane had already committed practically the same change in passing (commit 8e396a773), which also removed the server-side join. He therefore marked the entry withdrawn. Cary Huang's earlier concern about client-side memory use with very many publication tables was answered by Tom Lane as not significant compared to the per-table data pg_dump already collects.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'll mark this CF entry "withdrawn", since it wasn't rejected
exactly.  Too bad we don't have a classification of "superseded
by events", or something like that.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_dump --where option
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a --where option to pg_dump that exposes pg_dump's existing internal ability to filter dumped table data with a WHERE clause, building on an earlier patch. This version aims to give clearer error messages for invalid clauses and to apply a filter only to a specified table instead of to every table matched by a pattern.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Daniel Gustafsson's review raised open issues: pasting arbitrary SQL into the query without schema-qualification checks may expose CVE-2018-1058-style problems, the patch had no tests, and it was unclear how quoted multibyte table names or table names containing colons would be handled. The author did not answer this review for two weeks, and Michael Paquier, noting that tests are needed, marked the entry returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Documenting something is well and good, but isn't allowing arbitrary SQL
copy-pasted into the query (which isn't checked for schema qualification)
opening up for some of the ill-effects of CVE-2018-1058?

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_dump new feature: exporting functions only
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a pg_dump switch (--functions-only) to dump only stored functions and procedures from a database, without resolving their dependencies on other objects. During the discussion the design moved toward pattern-based include/exclude options per object type (e.g. --routine/--exclude-routine alongside --table, --schema, --extension).
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers asked for a different design: pattern-matching options per object type with matching exclude options, in line with --table and --extension, instead of an all-or-nothing --functions-only switch. The author summarised the new plan and said she would rewrite the patch, but no reworked patch is shown before the deadline. The committer closing the entry concluded that a different design was wanted and that it would not make v15.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Looks clear to me that a different design is wanted here, and that
this won't make it for v15, so I have marked the patch as returned
with feedback in the CF app.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_dump -C Grant statement on create database
precedents_retrieved.summary: When pg_dump is run with -C (emit CREATE DATABASE), it would also emit the database-level GRANT statements (such as GRANT CREATE ON DATABASE), matching what pg_dumpall already produces. The patch makes emitting these grants subject to the existing -x (no privileges) option.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The thread contains only the original report, a reply agreeing it is an oversight, and the patch submission; no review or objection to the patch appears, and the entry was returned with feedback about three months later.

precedents_retrieved.title: Ignore attributes of tables part of extensions in pg_dump
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change pg_dump so that getTableAttrs skips fetching column and type information for tables that are members of an extension, using the ext_member flag. The goal was to avoid gathering attributes for tables that pg_dump does not dump individually.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch. A reviewer asked why it checked ext_member rather than the usual dobj.dump flag. The author concluded that skipping attributes based on either flag would break binary upgrade, which still dumps extension member tables individually.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Hm. I have been pondering about this code more and I am dropping the patch as either adding a check based on the flag to track dumpable objects or ext_member visibly breaks the logic that binary upgrade and tables in extensions rely on.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix ALTER TABLE DROP EXPRESSION with ONLY option
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... DROP EXPRESSION work on inheritance trees with more than one level, where it now fails with "must be applied to child tables too". It adds a `!recursing` check in ATPrepDropExpression() so the ONLY check runs only for the table named in the command.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Peter Eisentraut asked why tablecmds.c passes recurse = false when recursing, and suggested a more consistent use of the two flags would make the existing code work. Tom Lane said that if the flags matter here, DROP EXPRESSION should not use ATSimpleRecursion. The author replied in December 2025 that v3 is correct, and no later reply appears before the entry was returned with feedback.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent rejects this idea. The one objection rests on the recorded coverage concern in P18 and P1, which message #7 raises and nobody has answered yet.
Other points from this angle do not hold up. The new ALTER TABLE ONLY ... SET EXPRESSION follows the existing pattern for separate defaults, and the multi-parent failure exists on master already.
Only pg_dump output changes. There is no new WAL, on-disk format, catalog column or protocol change. The one persistent-state concern is the catalog state that restore and pg_upgrade produce.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. pg_dump only emits ALTER TABLE ONLY ... SET EXPRESSION, which the table owner can already run, and a restore already evaluates generation expressions, so no new code runs as the restoring role. The loss of inherited CHECK and NOT NULL constraints is a data-integrity issue for other angles.
The goal itself, fixing silent loss of child generation expressions in pg_dump, is a clear bug fix and belongs in core. The objections above concern sequencing and maintainability only.

This is a pg_dump bugfix for silently wrong restores, and no existing feature, option or extension gives a correct dump of a child's differing generation expression. The patch extends the existing separate-ALTER mechanism used for defaults, so it does not add a second mechanism.

Demand is shown: this fixes a reported bug (#19773) where pg_dump restores a wrong generation expression without any error. Correct dump and restore is a core duty of pg_dump, a second developer was tracking the same defect (message #2), and the cost falls only on dumps that contain inherited generated columns.
